crm_notes:
Quick fragments from meetings and internal notes:
- Use-case: live product recommendations + conversational commerce (chat on checkout flow). Heavy real-time inference; embedding-based rerank for personalized results.
- Targets: throughput 200-300 qps peak, sustained baseline ~120 qps. SLOs: p50 token latency target <120ms for chat, p95 request latency <200ms, p99 <400ms. Availability target 99.95% with cross-region failover.
- Model preference: prefer quantized Llama2-70B variants for quality; fall back to 13B-quantized during capacity pressure. Must support model pinning per route.
- Routing needs: regional routing (na: us-east + us-west) with automatic failover to EU for redundancy during incidents. Warm-standby in EU with reserved headroom ~25%.
- Hardware ask: reserved GPU pool plan: US-East 6 GPUs reserved, US-West 4 GPUs reserved, EU-West 2 GPUs reserved (initial). Redwood recommended 3x headroom plan for peak burst; customer pushing for 25% headroom only.
- POC notes: batching and KV-cache improved throughput ~1.6x. Observed degrade when KV cache miss rate >40%.
- Security: KMS/HSM required for key custody, SAML SSO required for console access, audit logs retention 1 year. Data residency for EU customers.
- Pricing/procurement: procurement needs line-item invoice, term sheet, and sample SLA addendum. Procurement window ~6 weeks.
- Quote discussion: customer asking for 12-month committed reserved pool + option to scale dedicated capacity month-to-month for 1 quarter.
- Quote objections: wants clearer failure domain plan (AZ vs region), blackout maintenance windows and RTO expectations.
- Direct quote paraphrase: "We can tolerate some perf variance but not multi-hour outages — need deterministic failover and credits."
- Next internal: Arjun to deliver final sizing diagram (3/12), Lena to coordinate procurement docs, legal to review SLA addendum.
technical_requirements_summary: Reserved GPU planning across regions/AZs: multi-region pools with warm standby; recommend explicit AZ distribution (no single-AZ majority), 25% headroom baseline, autoscale burst to public capacity with fallback policies; route-by-latency with sticky session support for chat; KMS keywrap for model artifacts; per-route model pinning and versioning.
commercial_notes: Estimated ARR range based on initial reserved config. Customer prefers annual commit but wants option to expand. Negotiation points: SLA uptime target, credit calculation, scoped maintenance windows, and failover proof points (runbook + DR test schedule).
procurement_notes: Procurement contact: Melissa Tan (melissa.t@arborion-capacity.com). Need PO terms, billing to US entity. Procurement expects redlined contract in 2 weeks.
